model_meta.description: Conceptual model of a gear pump using a drive gear with more teeth than its meshing driven gear, with asymmetric gear tooth profiles.

subsystems.description: External source of drive that rotates the first gear; its specific implementation is not defined by the claims.
First gear receives drive and transmits rotation through contact of its teeth with the second gear. It has more teeth than the second gear.

Second gear rotates through contact with the first gear. Its tooth faces are asymmetric about the stated radial centerline; contact and non-contact faces are involutes, with greater curvature radius on the contact face, designed to provide an effectively thicker apex. Circumferential gaps extend inward beyond the non-contact curvature circle, while the contact-face curvature circle lies inward of the innermost gap portion. Claims 2 and 7 additionally specify a smaller outer diameter than the first gear.
Component associated with the second gear to create power when driven. The description identifies a generator or centrifugal pump as alternative examples; neither is required by the claim.
Housing mounts the drive gear and driven gear; fluid travels from inlet to outlet through spaces between the teeth as the gears rotate.

item_flows.name: Drive rotation
item_flows.notes: Mechanical drive supplied to the first gear.

item_flows.name: Gear-mesh rotation transfer
item_flows.notes: Tooth contact transfers rotation from the first gear to the second gear.

item_flows.name: Driven-gear component drive
item_flows.notes: The driven gear drives its associated component.

steps.description: The first gear is connected to a source of drive and receives rotation.
First-gear teeth contact the contact faces of the second-gear teeth, causing the second gear to rotate.
The first gear transfers rotation to the second gear through tooth contact.

actions.name: Transport fluid from inlet to outlet

steps.description: As the gears rotate, spaces between the teeth move hydraulic fluid from the housing inlet toward the housing outlet.
